findings.summary: The added rounds:M4.43 entry says '⚠️ THE MEASUREMENT IS SETTLED and cost two reviewers real work: production ran the 2x mutant twelve times (42% kills, bimodal 3/4, honest never below 6), tests ran it five, and production retracted its own earlier single-run report that had told me the floor fix held.' No recorded verdict supports that attribution, and I checked every verdict in .harness/review that mentions multipliedBy(2). (1) The twelve/42%/bimodal-3-4/honest-never-below-6 series is the TEST reviewer's, not production's, and it is seven runs, not twelve: TR-M4.17-3 (e8a3151c..., role test-reviewer, task M4.17) reads 'fastRate = 4, 3, 4, 4, 3 over five class-scoped runs -- failures 0, 1, 0, 0, 1 -- plus two full :sequencer:test runs (246 tests) at 1 failure then 0. Killed in 3 of 7 runs, survived in 4. The mutant is bimodal at 3/4 ... Clean honest values: 6 ...' -- 3 of 7 is 43%, and 'kills it about 40% of the time' is that finding's own headline. (2) Production's only 2x-mutant runs anywhere in this task are THREE, at the 2000ms window, in M4.43-R1d (68c71440...): 'I measured the same configuration in my own tree ... and got fast=6, fast=7, fast=7.' There is no twelve-run production series in the harness at all. (3) 'tests ran it five' double-counts the same test review: the five class-scoped runs ARE part of the seven the sentence has just credited to production. (4) The 'earlier single-run report that had told me the floor fix held' is also the test reviewer's and was not one run -- TR-M4.17-6 (3893ebde..., test-reviewer) reports 'the class alone green 5/5 on an idle machine with instrumented values fastRate=3 slowRate=0 every run -- the 2x mutant lands EXACTLY on the inclusive floor isBetween(3L, 30L)' -- and the retraction is TR-M4.17-3, the same role. So the roles are swapped, the run counts are unsupported, and the report characterised as single-run was five runs stated as five.
findings.failure_scenario: baselines/review.txt is committed and permanent, and this sentence is the corroboration offered for the entry's central assertion -- it says the measurement is SETTLED -- in the one file whose entire worth is that its entries are checkable. Nothing in the tree reproduces a twelve-run, 42% series, so a session auditing the escape (M4.15, M4's VERIFIED.md and milestone review, is the next open row, and review.md's two-round-cap rule takes its round figures from .harness rather than from prose) reads a measurement it cannot reconcile with the M4.41 note in this same commit ('measured killed 2 of 5 runs', '~40%') or with any verdict, and cannot tell which figure was run and which was arithmetic. That is precisely the defect this commit files three rows about -- a number reported as a measurement without the runs behind it, non-negotiable 4 -- committed inside the argument that narrates it, one entry below rounds:M4.17, which already records the same error twice. It also moves the error off the author: it credits production with nine runs it never made and hands it a 'single-run report' that was another role's five-run report, in a paragraph whose stated subject is 'WHAT DROVE THE ROUNDS WAS MY OWN DRAFTING'. One clause fixes it: name the role and the real series -- test review, five class-scoped plus two full-suite runs, 3 kills of 7, honest never below 6; production, three 2000ms runs at 6/7/7 -- or drop the counts and say only that both reviewers measured it.
findings.remedy: Replace the run counts with what the verdicts record, attributed to the role that ran them, or delete the counts and keep 'measured independently by both reviewers'.

findings.summary: The entry's per-round narrative does not match the recorded rounds, and labels one round twice. By .harness/review for task M4.43, in mtime order: 961791a8 (test-reviewer, changes-requested; TR-M4.43-1 is the remedy's doubled 'honest ~13, mutant ~6' numbers) is round 1; 68c71440 (reviewer, changes-requested; R1a 'the two minors', R1b the production duplicate) is round 2; 0d447714 (test pass, reviewer changes-requested; R2a 'the mutant is 7, not 6' and 'BOTH ROWS') is round 3; b0a1c839 (both pass; R3a/R3b) is round 4. The entry puts 'the two minors' at Round 1 and the remedy at Round 2 -- inverted, and demonstrably so, since the remedy fix is already present in the bytes the two-minors round reviewed (R1d quotes the post-fix 'Measured at a 2000ms window ... So the mutant is 7, not 6'). It then uses 'Round 3' for two different rounds: for the 7-not-6/BOTH-ROWS findings (0d447714), and again in 'round 3 passed both roles but returned two new minors, both introduced by round 2's fixes', which describes b0a1c839. 0d447714 did not pass both roles -- its reviewer verdict is changes-requested carrying major M4.43-R2a -- and R3a/R3b were introduced by the fix to R2a, i.e. by the round the entry itself calls 3, not by round 2's fixes. Four recorded rounds are narrated as three.
findings.failure_scenario: Bounded, which is why it is minor: the do-not-split argument holds under any ordering, and the authoritative round count is computed from .harness, not read from this file, so no session is sent to do wrong work. The cost falls on the reader of the permanent record. review.md's two-round-cap rule treats these entries as the evidence for what the escape costs, and spends twenty lines on the tree having contradicted itself about exactly this kind of count; this entry asserts twice that counting is the thing that goes stale, and then reproduces a counting error in its own round labels. Someone reconciling 'round 3 passed both roles' with the changes-requested verdict at the hash the same paragraph called round 3 has to open .harness to learn which sentence to believe. Fix is renumbering the four rounds and moving the remedy clause ahead of the two-minors clause.
findings.remedy: Number the four recorded rounds 1-4 in hash order, with the remedy/doubled-numbers finding first and the passing round last.
